R148.note: Removes the stray [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] so the app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter applies; no other behaviour change.

R149.note: Standard PreparedStatement/setString parameterization replacing string-concatenated Statement query; no other change.

R150.note: GetFullPath+StartsWith containment check alone closes the vector; the added file.Contains("..") substring rejection is an extra restriction not needed to close it and could reject a legitimate filename that merely contains a literal '..' substring.

R151.note: OWASP Encode.forHtml wraps the JSP scriptlet output; matches project's documented CWE-79/java doctrine, no other change.

R152.note: keyfunc now rejects non-RSA signing methods before returning the key, correctly closing the algorithm-confusion vector; no other change.

R153.note: Narrow JobRequest DTO for gob.Decode plus server-side isAdmin from a clearly-marked TODO stub matches the contract (Command/Priority still decoded and run, IsAdmin decided independently); gob ignores decoder-absent fields so legitimate payloads decode unchanged.

R154.note: Resolve-then-normalize-then-startsWith ordering correctly matches the stated contract; explanation's claim about resolve() treating absolute strings as relative is factually wrong but the containment check catches escapes regardless, so the fix itself is unaffected.

R155.note: AST-walk allowlisting +,-,*,/ (plus //,% which is a harmless superset) over declared variables matches the stated contract; undefined names and other syntax raise ValueError as required.

R156.note: f-string SQL replaced with text() + bound :date_filter parameter; standard SQLAlchemy Core parameterization, no other change.

R157.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) is the idiomatic bounded replacement for strlen on a non-guaranteed-terminated fixed buffer; NUL-containing names report existing length and unterminated names return the bound (16) rather than overreading, matching the contract's safety intent.

R158.note: Single bounded snprintf with explicit truncation check (return -1) replaces strcpy/strcat, exactly matching the stated contract of rejecting oversized input rather than truncating.

R159.note: unserialize($payload, ['allowed_classes'=>false]) is the project's own documented canonical PHP CWE-502 fix and blocks all gadget-chain object instantiation; empty/invalid cookies and legitimate array-shaped cart data behave as before. Contract's literal phrase 'no longer reach unserialize()' isn't met verbatim (the call still runs on attacker bytes) but no signing mechanism exists anywhere in the shown code to build against, and the RCE vector is closed.

R160.note: Tika magic-byte detection correctly replaces the trust in the client Content-Type header and closes the CWE-434 finding; the added mandatory ImageIO decode/re-encode step is extra hardening against the same weakness class that could reject some genuinely valid images ImageIO cannot parse (e.g., CMYK JPEGs) without flagging that trade-off.

R161.note: Bounds check now uses segment.size() (the span's real capacity) instead of the untrusted claimedCapacity, correctly closing the OOB write; claimedCapacity is left as an unused vestigial parameter rather than removed as the contract suggests, but this is dead code, not a behavioural change.

R162.note: DB::select with ? placeholder and bound array replaces string-concatenated SQL; standard Laravel parameterization, no other change.

R163.note: createElement/textContent DOM construction replaces innerHTML template literal, preserving identical DOM structure and visual output for benign input while removing the injection surface.
